notes: key_material_provider (ADR-0140): AsyncKeyBundle v1 omits provider-visible acs_generation/acs_state_hash. The provider still sees stable subject_device_id, provider_pool_id, timing and inventory shape, but the protocol no longer gives it an account-wide ACS correlator. Authorization is checked by the fetcher against relationship-pinned trusted ACS/DeviceCredential state.

cross_profile_linkage (ADR-0129 rule 14): a native per-app push token presented for two IdentityProfiles links them at the push provider unless vendor push is disabled for a Keep-separate profile or one declared gateway is used; on web each profile has its own Web Push subscription.

descriptor_mailbox_linkage and contact_graph_edge on Home roles (ADR-0130 rule 4, F-R4-4): one operator running the discovery publisher, IntroGate and mailbox can link the published contact identity (alias, intro identity) to every deposit and drain, and sees contact edges among its co-resident users (the same client address or session drains one mailbox and deposits into another). 'sometimes' means: whenever those roles or those contacts share one operator.

ratchet_header_shape (ADR-0131 rule 4): OM-Crypto-v1 does not encrypt the Double Ratchet header. The mailbox-class Homes that carry a 1:1 envelope see the header OM-CBOR [crypto_profile, ratchet public key (32 B), pn, n] and its length: they can count messages per ratchet chain and see DH-ratchet turns. No identity is in the header. Header encryption needs a new CryptoProfile.

shared_blob_linkage (ADR-0129 rule 10): the default per-send encryption gives every send a fresh content key, so the same asset has a different BlobID in each conversation. Only the opt-in shared-blob mode for expressive assets (stickers, custom emoji) reuses one BlobID, and then the BlobStore can link those conversations by it.

lan_observer (R-270, R-271): the LAN advertisement has a fixed number of rendezvous tags per epoch. Real tags exist only for contacts marked for local mode; the rest are padding. Tags and, where available, the link-layer address rotate every epoch, and a tag is retired when its relationship ends or is blocked. The observer learns that an OM device is present, not how many contacts it has or which advertisements across epochs are the same device.

key_material_provider: subject_device_id remains constant for a device and is therefore an always-stable device correlator. It no longer automatically groups several devices into one account; any account/contact linkage is deployment/traffic dependent rather than a bundle-wire property (ADR-0140).

provider-resource authentication (ADR-0138): routine provider administration uses independent opaque capabilities rather than device_auth; repeated use may link the same provider resource but does not expose a DeviceCredential/DeviceID. Mailbox RecoveryRequest fan-out is separate and exposes the request AccountID plus recovery-attempt fact for that operation.

replaceable Android wake (ADR-0152): FCM, UnifiedPush-compatible gateways/distributors and other push adapters are modeled as push_provider boundaries with opaque wake timing/token/profile-linkage exposure; a persistent encrypted relay/Home wake/fetch connection is observed by that relay/Home rather than inventing a privileged push authority. Adapter switching never changes canonical message/identity state. ADR-0153: obsolete registrations are retired where possible; if provider-side retirement cannot be confirmed, residual token/profile-linkage retention is provider-defined unless an enforceable finite lease is explicitly declared, and the obsolete handle remains wake-only rather than fetch/account authority.
